summary: Route selection score rounding caused subset of requests to egress via secondary region with high streaming p99
description:
Issue summary: Beginning 2026-03-12 09:10 UTC, a subset of streaming inference requests from customer Streambean Analytics experienced elevated p95/p99 tail latency and occasional streaming stalls. Initial symptoms looked like cross-region egress to eu-west for sessions that normally use us-east, increasing TTFB and triggering client-side timeouts.

Impact: Affects ~4% of Streambean's traffic on their dedicated pool; observable p99 increase from ~220ms to ~1.6s for streaming start, and intermittent partial payloads/stream reconnects. Customer reports user-visible delays in live transcript and webhook timeouts.

Environment: Production, dedicated capacity for Streambean Analytics (customer_id sbn-224). Edge nodes in us-east showed healthy health checks; routing decisions show repeated selection of eu-west egress for some account-tagged requests.

Requested action: Triage routing decision logic, confirm rollback or mitigation, provide ETA for permanent fix and post-incident action items.
impact: Customer-facing latency regressions on streaming endpoints leading to transcript delays and occasional client reconnects. Business impact: degraded demo/live usage for Streambean (dedicated).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use Streambean account token (account tag sbn-224) to open streaming chat session against streaming endpoint using model gpt-open-13b-v1.
2) Send initial prompt with ~80 token system and call stream; observe TTFB and streaming start time in client.
3) Repeat across 100 sessions around 2026-03-12 09:00-10:30 UTC time window. ~4% of sessions will show >1.2s TTFB and occasional stalled chunk after first 3-5 tokens.
4) On platform side, query route decision logs for request IDs; look for route_score and selected_egress_region fields.
logs: 2026-03-12T09:13:21Z request_id=req-8f3a route_score_primary=0.4999 route_score_secondary=0.5001 selected_egress=eu-west latency_connect=760ms streaming_start=1.42s
2026-03-12T09:17:03Z request_id=req-b1c2 route_score_primary=0.5000 route_score_secondary=0.5000 selected_egress=us-east latency_connect=210ms streaming_start=0.22s
2026-03-12T09:21:55Z request_id=req-cc4d route_score_primary=0.4998 route_score_secondary=0.5002 selected_egress=eu-west latency_connect=1.02s streaming_start=1.60s
Edge proxy metrics: us-east egress success rate 99.98%, eu-west success rate 99.95% (no health alarms).
Tracing sample: route-eval-v2 module returned floating score values; downstream selection picks highest score with no stable tie-breaker.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: path/flap causing normal tie-break behavior to favor eu-west. Network team found no BGP or peering anomalies during window.

Observability: rolling deployment of 'route-eval-v2' change went live 2026-03-11 22:00 UTC with a code change that moves scores from integer buckets to normalized floats and updated rounding logic in router.

Reproducible pattern: accounts with high short-burst session rate produce route_score values that land very close to 0.5, and the new rounding exposed a bias that prefers secondary when scores are tied within floating epsilon.
Confirmed by sim: running production traffic samples through local routing binary reproduces ~3.8% misrouted-to-secondary ratio matching customer percent.
Observability gap: no explicit metric for 'tie_break_bias', added temporary histogram for route_score delta distribution and egress selection ratio per account.
comments: Lucas Ortega (Support) 2026-03-12: Notified customer and created ticket. Provided workaround: pin account to us-east by setting account routing override. Customer accepted temporary workaround.
SRE (Evan Ross) 2026-03-12: Verified network paths and peering; no network-level cause. Pointed to recent routing-service change. Linking PR for review.

Routing Eng (Priya Patel) 2026-03-13: Identified tie-breaker rounding change as root cause. Proposed two options: 1) hotfix to deterministic tie-break (prefer primary when delta < 1e-6), 2) rollback to integer-bucket behavior.
resolution:
Hotfix deployed 2026-03-13 18:30 UTC: routing-service v2.1.7 patched to include deterministic tie-break rule (prefer primary when score delta < 1e-5) and metric instrumentation added. Immediate effect: Streambean misroute ratio dropped to <0.1% and streaming p99 returned to baseline within 30 minutes.

Follow-ups assigned: ENG-ops ticket to add automated canary gating for routing logic changes (backlog item), alert rule for route selection skew >0.5% on account-level, and postmortem documenting rollout gap and observability shortfall. Customer compensated per SLA and notified.
